text_blocks.snippet: The Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program forgives the remaining balance of your federal student loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments (10 years) while working full-time for a qualifying employer. There is no limit to the amount of forgiveness you can receive under PSLF, meaning the full remaining balance of your eligible federal student loans can be forgiven, even if it's a large amount.

list.title: Qualifying Payments:
list.snippet: To qualify for PSLF, you must make 120 monthly payments on your federal student loans while working full-time for a qualifying employer.

list.title: Qualifying Employers:
list.snippet: These include government organizations (federal, state, local, or tribal) and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations.

list.title: Repayment Plans:
list.snippet: You must be on an income-driven repayment (IDR) plan or the Standard Repayment Plan for at least 10 years.

list.title: No Loan Limit:
list.snippet: There is no cap on the amount of debt that can be forgiven through PSLF as long as you meet the requirements, according to the Federal Student Aid website.

list.title: Biden Administration Adjustments:
list.snippet: Under the Biden administration, significant changes and improvements have been made to the PSLF program, leading to a substantial increase in the number of borrowers receiving forgiveness.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: The Department of Education reports that as of January 14, 2025, $78.46 billion in student loans has been forgiven for 1,069,000 borrowers through PSLF, according to NerdWallet.

list.title: Average Forgiveness:
